recognize_zh: 抹片中大量細胞核呈雙葉、摺疊或腎形（butterfly／bilobed nucleus），染色質細緻，細胞質淡藍且幾乎沒有顆粒，成片出現，這是低顆粒型 APL（hypogranular／microgranular variant）的典型形態。
features: Sheets of medium to large cells with bilobed, folded, reniform or 'butterfly' nuclei
Fine, delicate chromatin with nuclear grooves and overlapping lobes
Moderate amounts of pale gray-blue cytoplasm with sparse or no visible granules
No Auer rods clearly visible in this field
High cell density with many smudged/crushed cells; normal neutrophils not evident
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a markedly increased population of medium to large cells with bilobed, folded or reniform nuclei, fine chromatin and moderate pale cytoplasm that is largely devoid of visible granules. Auer rods are not clearly identified in this field, and mature neutrophils are sparse. The nuclear configuration with hypogranular cytoplasm and high white cell count is characteristic of the hypogranular (microgranular) variant of acute promyelocytic leukemia, which can be mistaken for monocytic leukemia. Findings are consistent with hypogranular acute promyelocytic leukemia; strong MPO positivity and PML::RARA confirmation are expected, and coagulopathy should be evaluated urgently.

ddx.vs: Promonocytes have folded nuclei too, but are MPO weak/negative, NSE strongly positive and HLA-DR/CD14/CD64 positive, whereas hypogranular APL is strongly MPO-positive and HLA-DR negative.
Cup-like blasts can resemble folded nuclei and are CD34/HLA-DR negative, but lack PML::RARA and usually show less intense MPO staining.

ddx.dx: Sézary cells or T-cell lymphoma in leukemic phase
ddx.vs: Cerebriform nuclei have condensed chromatin and scant cytoplasm and are MPO negative with T-cell markers.
